Senses.Explanation: Able to act, come and go, or respond without constraint: free and at ease, at liberty, or freely. The word is attested 4,537 times in 388 allowlisted texts. Foyan Qingyuan closes an address by telling everyone to drink tea in the hall, free and at ease (堂中喫茶，自由自在). Yunmen Wenyan says that only upon arriving here can one roll up and extend freely, with response and function unimpaired (卷舒自在，應用無虧). The Yongzheng Emperor uses the result phrase “obtain great freedom” (獲大自在), while Zhean Jingfan says “unconstrained and unbound in every place; without fault at every time” (一切處自在無繫，一切時無所過患). Dahui Zonggao says that one then enters birth and death and obtains great freedom (出生入死得大自在). Other records pair freedom in birth and death with freedom in coming and going, and explicitly test whether freedom at death matches ordinary freedom amid encountered objects. Zen bends an everyday freedom word into public tests about response, movement, birth, and death, while Baizhang Huaihai warns against casually declaring a buddha free or not free. Adjective, adverb, result noun, and the repeated form “free and at ease” remain grammatical deployments of the same condition.
Senses.Note: Counted constructions: “free and at ease,” 185; “free and unobstructed,” 50; “obtain great freedom,” 258; and “not at ease,” 134. The 278 occurrences of the larger title-name translated “Contemplating Freely,” and personal names such as Yun Zizai, are proper-name uses and are not merged into this adjectival sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 各自大家堂中喫茶自由自在
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄): inside the Upper-Hall Record of Foyan Qingyuan at Longmen, Foyan ends the exchange by telling everyone to drink tea freely and at ease in the hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 到這裏始能卷舒自在，應用無虧
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Yunmen Wenyan as the speaker of this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 境智融通，色空無礙，獲大自在
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄): in his imperially authored general preface, the Yongzheng Emperor describes the second barrier as the interpenetration of object and knowledge and of form and emptiness, obtaining great freedom.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一切處自在無繫，一切時無所過患。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhean Jingfan (蔗菴範禪師語錄): in his Guzisheng Monastery hall address, Zhean Jingfan describes being free and unbound in every place and without fault at every time.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao says that one then enters birth and death and obtains great freedom.

Occurrences.Kwic: 便乃一切時一切處。任運自在。應用無方。諸人還委悉麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄), in Hongzhi Zhengjue's opening-hall address at Jiangzhou Nengren: Hongzhi Zhengjue says, ‘At every time and in every place, proceed freely and at ease, responding without fixed direction,’ then asks whether the assembly understands.

Occurrences.Kwic: 透得一句生死自在；透得二句來去自由；三句透得，可以為人天師；四句總透得，可以為佛祖師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Wuming of Shouchang (壽昌無明和尚語錄): Wuming Huijing says that penetrating one of four phrases gives freedom in birth and death, two gives freedom in coming and going, and all four allows one to be teacher of buddhas and patriarchs.

Occurrences.Kwic: 當知欲驗臨終受生自在不自在，但驗尋常行心於塵境自由不自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), Guifeng Zongmi section. Guifeng Zongmi is the exact speaker who says that freedom at death is tested by whether one's ordinary conduct is free amid encountered objects.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛秖是去住自由，不同眾生。佛不是虗空受苦，何得不苦？若說不苦，此語違負。等閑莫說，錯說佛神通自在不自在。具慙愧人，不敢說佛是有為是無為，不敢說佛自由不自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record (天聖廣燈錄): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Baizhang Huaihai as the speaker of this occurrence.
